Rashi on Pesachim 41b:10:1.hebrew: ואל תתמה שהרי הותר מכללו אצל צלי - דהא אפילו צלי היה אסור לאכול ביום, כדכתיב: "ואכלו את הבשר בלילה הזה", ולא ביום, וכשחשכה הותר מכלל איסור עשה דצלי. ונימא נמי: נהי דלא הותר לכתחלה אצל נא, מיהו לא לחייב עליה אם אכלו:
Rashi on Pesachim 41b:10:1.english: And do not be confounded, as it was permitted from its general rule with regard to roasted [meat] - For even roasted [meat] was forbidden to be eaten during the day, as it is written: "And they shall eat the flesh in that night," and not during the day, and when it grew dark, it was permitted from the general prohibition of the positive commandment regarding roasted [meat]. So let us say also: granted that it was not permitted initially with regard to partially roasted [meat], nevertheless one should not be liable for it if he ate it.

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:11:1.english: As [there is] no [need for] the verse to state: “but roasted with fire” - For it is written above it [in the preceding verse]: “roasted with fire, and unleavened bread,” etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:12:1.english: I [could] read “boiled” [bashel] - It would have sufficed for you with the reading of bashel.

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:12:2.hebrew: אין לי - שיתחייב על אכילת בשר אלא אם כן בישלו משחשיכה, שהוא עיקר זמנו:
Rashi on Pesachim 41b:12:2.english: I have only - That one is liable for eating [the] meat only if he boiled it after dark, which is its primary time.

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:12:3.english: [If] he boiled it while it was still day - and ate it after dark, from where [is this derived]?

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:13:1.english: But he [already] used it - Rabbi himself expounded it above for other liquids and for pot-roasting.

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:13:2.hebrew: בשל מבושל - מדשני בדבוריה, דריש ביה דרשה אחריתי נמי:
Rashi on Pesachim 41b:13:2.english: Bashel mevushal [boiled] - Since [Scripture] varied its wording, he derives from it another exposition as well.

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:15:1.english: An olive-bulk [of] roasted [meat] while it is still day, he is liable - [The Gemara] explains it below.

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:16:1.english: Taught - [That is,] the liability for roasted [meat] while it is still day [is] similar to the liability for partially roasted [meat] after dark.

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:1:1.hebrew: לוקה שתים - משום "לא תאכל נא" ומשום "לא תאכלו כי אם צלי אש", ד"כי אם צלי אש" נמי אלאו ד"לא תאכלו" קאי:
Rashi on Pesachim 41b:1:1.english: He receives two [sets of lashes] - For [transgressing] "You shall not eat [it] partially roasted" and for "You shall not eat, except roasted with fire" [Exodus 12:9], because "except roasted with fire" also refers to the negative prohibition of "You shall not eat."

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:1:2.english: [One who eats it] boiled receives two [sets of lashes] - On account of [the prohibition against eating it] boiled, and on account of [the verse], "You shall not eat [of it...] except roasted with fire."

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:2:1.english: It is a prohibition stated in general terms - For it includes within it all types of cooking that are not roasting, to prohibit [them].

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:3:1.hebrew: איכא דאמרי תרתי הוא דלא לקי - כיון שהוא לוקה משום נא, משום מבושל, תו לא לקי משום כלל דכי אם צלי אש:
Rashi on Pesachim 41b:3:1.english: Some say: It is two [sets of lashes] that he does not receive - Since he receives lashes for [eating it] raw [or] for [eating it] boiled, he does not additionally receive lashes for the general [prohibition] of "except roasted with fire."

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:3:2.hebrew: אבל חדא מיהא לקי - כגון המבשל בחמי טבריא ואכלו, דאין כאן מלקות דבישול ולא מלקות של נא, לוקה משום כי אם צלי אש:
Rashi on Pesachim 41b:3:2.english: But at any rate one [set of lashes] he does receive - For example, one who cooks [it] in the hot springs of Tiberias and eats it, where there are neither lashes for cooking nor lashes for [eating it] partially roasted, he receives lashes on account of "except roasted with fire."

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:4:1.hebrew: ואיכא דאמרי חדא נמי לא לקי - משום כי אם צלי אש, דלא מיוחד לאויה דידיה כלאו דחסימה, שהוא מפרש איסורו, וסמיכא ליה פרשת מלקות לעיל מיניה:
Rashi on Pesachim 41b:4:1.english: And some say [that] he does not receive even one [set of lashes] - because of [the phrase] "except roasted with fire" [Exodus 12:9], since its prohibition is not specific like the prohibition of muzzling [Deuteronomy 25:4], which specifies its prohibition, and the passage [concerning] lashes is juxtaposed to it above it.

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:5:1.hebrew: אכל זג לוקה שתים - נזיר שאכלו: משום זג לא יאכל, ומשום מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין מחרצנים וגו, דלא יאכל קאי נמי אמכל אשר יעשה:
Rashi on Pesachim 41b:5:1.english: [If] he ate a grape skin, he receives two [sets of lashes] - A nazirite who ate it [is liable]: [one] on account of "a grape skin he shall not eat," and [one] on account of "of anything that is made of the grapevine, from pressed grapes, etc.," for "he shall not eat" also refers to "of anything that is made."

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:6:1.hebrew: לאו שבכללות - אין לוקין על "מכל אשר יעשה", דלאו שבכללות הוא, שכולל חרצנים וזגים, וענבים לחים ויבשים, ועלים ולולבין:
Rashi on Pesachim 41b:6:1.english: A prohibition stated in general terms - One does not receive lashes for [violating] "from anything that is made [of the grapevine]," for it is a prohibition stated in general terms, as it includes seeds and skins, and fresh and dried grapes, and leaves and shoots.

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:6:2.hebrew: תרתי לא לקי - היכא דאכל זג או חרצן ולקי עלייהו, לא לקי תו משום "מכל אשר יעשה". ומודה אביי דאם אכל זג וחרצן, לוקה שתים, דכיון דמפורש כל אחד לעצמו, קאי נמי אלאו ד"לא יאכל", והוי כמאן דכתב לאו אכל חד וחד. והכי מוכח במסכת נזיר, דלא פליג אביי אלא אמלקות ד"מכל אשר יעשה":
Rashi on Pesachim 41b:6:2.english: He does not receive two [sets of lashes] - Where he ate a grape skin or a grape seed and receives lashes for them, he does not receive lashes in addition on account of "from anything that is made" [of the grapevine]. And Abaye concedes that if he ate [both] a grape skin and a grape seed, he receives two [sets of] lashes, for since each one is specified on its own, [the prohibition] of "he shall not eat" also applies to it, and it is as though a [separate] prohibition were written for each and every one. And so it is proven in Tractate Nazir, that Abaye only disagrees regarding the lashes of "from anything that is made".

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:6:3.hebrew: חדא מיהא לקי - אם אכל עלין ולולבין, דאין כאן מלקות דזג וחרצן, לקי משום לאו ד"מכל אשר יעשה":
Rashi on Pesachim 41b:6:3.english: At any rate, he receives one [set of lashes] - If he ate leaves and shoots, where there are no lashes for skin and seed, he receives lashes on account of the prohibition of "from anything that is made [of the grapevine]."

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:7:1.english: [If] one ate a partially roasted olive-bulk while it was still day, [he is] exempt - [The Gemara] explains the reason later from verses.

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:7:2.hebrew: לא פסל את עצמו מבני חבורה - דאמרי' לקמן (פסחים דף פו.): אין הפסח נאכל לא בשתי חבורות כאחד, ואין האוכל אוכל בשני מקומות, ונפקא לן מ"בבית אחד יאכל", ומתרגמינן: "בחבורא חדא יתאכל". ואכילה דמבעוד יום לאו אכילה היא, ומותר לאכול משתחשך עם בני חבורה שנמנה עמהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 41b:7:2.english: He has not disqualified himself from [the] members of [his] group - For we say later (Pesachim 86a): The Paschal lamb may not be eaten by two groups at once, nor may one who eats [it] eat in two places; and we derive this from "In one house shall it be eaten," which we translate [in Aramaic as] "In one group shall it be eaten." And eating while it is still day is not [considered] eating, and he is permitted to eat after dark with the members of the group with whom he was registered.

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:7:3.english: A roasted olive-bulk after dark - from the Paschal [lamb] upon which he was registered.

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:7:4.hebrew: פסל עצמו מבני חבורה - כדפרישית, שאין האוכל מותר לאכול הימנו בשני מקומות:
Rashi on Pesachim 41b:7:4.english: He has disqualified himself from the group - As I explained, for one who eats [it] is not permitted to eat of it in two places.

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:8:1.hebrew: בשעה שאינו בקום אכול צלי - דאין לו היתר אכילת צלי, אינו דין שישנו בלאו דלא תאכל נא:
Rashi on Pesachim 41b:8:1.english: At a time when he is not [included] in “arise, eat roasted” - [That is,] when he does not have permission to eat roasted [meat], is it not logical that he is [included] in the prohibition of “do not eat [it] partially roasted”?

Rashi on Pesachim 41b:9:1.hebrew: או לא - או לא נאמר כן, אלא בענין אחר: בשעה שישנו בקום אכול צלי — דהיינו בלילה, דכתיב: "ואכלו את הבשר בלילה הזה" — אינו בבל תאכל נא:
Rashi on Pesachim 41b:9:1.english: Or not - Or [perhaps] we do not say so, but rather in another way: at the time when one is [included] in "arise [and] eat [it] roasted" — which is at night, as it is written: "And they shall eat the flesh in that night" — he is not [included] in "do not eat [it] partially roasted."

Tosafot on Pesachim 41b:11:1.hebrew: שאין ת"ל כי אם צלי אש - אע"ג דאיצטריך להלקות עליו משום כי אם צלי אש, היינו נמי משום דסמכיה לנא ומבושל:
Tosafot on Pesachim 41b:11:1.english: "As there is no need for the verse to state: 'But roasted with fire'" - Even though [this phrase] is needed to administer lashes for it on account of "but roasted with fire," that is also because [Scripture] juxtaposed it to "partially roasted and boiled."

Tosafot on Pesachim 41b:14:1.hebrew: אם כן לימא קרא בשל בשל או מבושל מבושל - הכא משמע דאורחיה דקרא לכפול תיבה אחת בענין אחד טפי מבשני עניינים, וכן במרובה (ב"ק דף סה.) גבי "המצא תמצא", ובהחובל (שם דף פה:) גבי "ורפא ירפא". וקשה, דבריש היו בודקין (סנהדרין ד"מ:) קאמר: מדהוי ליה למיכתב "דרוש תדרוש" או "חקור תחקור", וכתב "היטב" — שמע מינה לאפנויי; משמע דאי הוה כתב הכי, לא הוה מופנה. ושמא התם לא חש לדקדק בלשון, רק להוכיח דמופנה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 41b:14:1.english: "If so, let the verse say 'bashel bashel' or 'mevushal mevushal'" - Here it implies that it is the manner of Scripture to repeat one word in a single form rather than in two forms, and similarly in [the chapter] Merubah (Bava Kamma 65a) regarding "himatze timatze," and in [the chapter] HaChovel (there, 85b) regarding "verapo yerape." And this is difficult, for at the beginning of [the chapter] Hayu Bodkin (Sanhedrin 40b) [the Gemara] says: "Since it could have written 'darosh tidrosh' or 'chakor tachkor,' and it wrote 'heitev' [thoroughly], learn from this that [it is written] to render [the verse] free [for exegesis]"; this implies that if it had written thus, it would not have been free [for exegesis]. And perhaps there [the Gemara] was not concerned to be exact in its phrasing, only to prove that [the verse] is free [for exegesis].

Tosafot on Pesachim 41b:1:1.hebrew: אכל כזית נא לוקה שתים משום נא ומשום כי אם צלי אש דהוי כאילו כתיב אל תאכלו כי אם צלי אש - הקשה הרר"י דאורלינ"ש: אמאי חשבי' בריש אלו נערות (כתובות דף ל.) בעולה לכהן גדול בעשה גרידא, ד"כי אם בתולה מעמיו" כתיב? הא כי היכי דחשבינן הכא "כי אם צלי אש" בלאו, ה"נ ה"ל לאיחשובי בעולה לכהן גדול בלאו, דהוי כאילו כתיב "לא יקח כי אם בתולה"! וי"ל, ד"כי אם בתולה" לא חשיב לאו, משום דסיפא דקרא מוכח עליו דהוי עשה, דכתיב: "כי אם בתולה מעמיו יקח אשה":
Tosafot on Pesachim 41b:1:1.english: [One who] ate an olive-bulk [of it] partially roasted receives two [sets of] lashes, [one] on account of "partially roasted" and [one] on account of "except roasted with fire," for it is as if it is written, "Do not eat [it] except roasted with fire" - Rabbi Y. of Orléans raised a difficulty: Why do we reckon at the beginning of [the chapter] Elu Ne'arot (Ketubot 30a) [the prohibition of] a non-virgin to a High Priest as merely a positive commandment, since it is written, "except a virgin from his people"? Surely, just as we reckon here "except roasted with fire" as a negative prohibition, so too should [the prohibition of] a non-virgin to a High Priest be reckoned as a negative prohibition, since it is as if it is written, "He shall not take [any] except a virgin"! And one can answer that "except a virgin" is not reckoned as a negative prohibition because the end of the verse proves concerning it that it is a positive commandment, as it is written: "except a virgin from his people shall he take [as] a wife."

Tosafot on Pesachim 41b:3:1.hebrew: איכא דאמרי חדא מיהא לקי - פ"ה: בחי וחמי טבריא חייב משום "כי אם צלי אש". וקשה לר"ת: א"כ, בין לאביי בין לרבא תיקשי להו ברייתא דלעיל, דתניא: "נא ומבושל אמרתי לך, ולא חי" — אלמא לא לקי על חי! ועוד, דאמר בפ' המקבל (ב"מ דף קטו:) אפלוגתא דרב הונא ורב יהודה בחובל ריחים ורכב, דרב יהודה אמר לוקה שתים ורב הונא אמר לוקה שלש, ומסיק רבא: "אנא דאמרי אפילו כרב יהודה; עד כאן לא קאמר רב יהודה התם אלא ד'כי נפש הוא חובל' לדברים אחרים הוא דאתא, אבל הכא 'כי אם צלי אש' למאי אתא?" ולפ"ה, הא איצטריך לחי ולחמי טבריא! לכ"נ לר"ת, דאחי לא לקי לכו"ע, ד"כי אם צלי אש" לא משמע דאתא למלקות אלא לעשה, ד"כי אם צלי אש תאכלו". ולא דמי ל"כי נפש הוא חובל", דבההוא מודו כו"ע דלוקה אשאר דברים, כדקתני התם בהדיא בברייתא: "חבל זוג של ספרים וצמד של פרות — לוקה שתים", ד"כי נפש הוא חובל" משמע שפיר בלשון לאו, שהוא נתינת טעם: כל שהוא דבר נפש לא תחבול. ואתא שפיר הא דקאמר רבא התם ד"כי נפש הוא חובל" אתא לשאר דברים, אבל "כי אם צלי אש" לא אתא אלא לעשה. וב"נא" ו"מבושל" דווקא פליגי; דרבא סבר: להכי סמכיה לאלו ללקות עליו על נא ומבושל שהם בני מילקא, ואביי אמר: אין לוקין על לאו שבכללות. והא דקאמר "חדא מיהת מילקא לקי", הכי פי': אם התרו בו משום "כי אם צלי אש" לבדו לוקה, אבל על מלקות נא ומבושל לא ילקה, דלהכי מהני מה שכתבו בלשון כלל; ומיהו לבדו מיהא לקי, שסמכו לאלו שהם בני מלקות:
Tosafot on Pesachim 41b:3:1.english: "Some say ... at any rate he receives one [set of lashes]" - Rashi explains: For raw [meat] and [meat cooked in] the hot springs of Tiberias, one is liable on account of "except roasted with fire." And this is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam: If so, both according to Abaye and according to Rava, the baraita above poses a difficulty for them, as it is taught: "Na [partially roasted] and boiled I told you, and not raw (chai)" — thus one does not receive lashes for raw [meat]! And furthermore, it is stated in Perek HaMekabel (Bava Metzia 115b) regarding the dispute between Rav Huna and Rav Yehudah concerning one who takes the lower and upper millstones as a pledge — where Rav Yehudah says he receives two [sets of] lashes and Rav Huna says he receives three [sets of] lashes — and Rava concludes: "I say [my view holds] even according to Rav Yehudah; Rav Yehudah only stated [his view] there because 'for he takes a life as a pledge' comes [to include] other things [that sustain life], but here, what does 'except roasted with fire' come for?" Now according to Rashi's explanation, it is indeed needed for raw [meat] and [meat cooked in] the hot springs of Tiberias! Therefore, it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that for raw [meat] he does not receive lashes according to everyone, for "except roasted with fire" does not imply that it comes for lashes, but rather for a positive commandment, [namely,] "except roasted with fire shall you eat [it]." And it is not similar to "for he takes a life as a pledge," for in that case everyone agrees that he receives lashes for other things, as it is explicitly taught there in the baraita: "If one took a barber's shears or a yoke of oxen as a pledge, he receives two [sets of] lashes," because "for he takes a life as a pledge" well implies a negative prohibition, as it is giving a reason: anything that is a matter of life [sustenance], you shall not take as a pledge. And thus fits well what Rava says there, that "for he takes a life as a pledge" comes for other things, whereas "except roasted with fire" comes only for a positive commandment. And it is specifically regarding "na [partially roasted] and boiled" that they disagree: for Rava holds that for this reason [Scripture] juxtaposed it to those [prohibitions] — in order to incur lashes for it on account of "na and boiled," which are subject to lashes; whereas Abaye says one does not receive lashes for a generalized prohibition (lav shebichlalot). And as for what [the Gemara] says, "at any rate he receives one [set of] lashes," this is its explanation: if they warned him on account of "except roasted with fire" alone, [he receives lashes]; however, in addition to the lashes for "na and boiled" he does not receive lashes, for this is what writing it in generalized language accomplishes; nevertheless, [when warned] on its own at any rate he does receive lashes, since [Scripture] juxtaposed it to those [prohibitions] which are subject to lashes.

Tosafot on Pesachim 41b:5:1.hebrew: אמר רבא אכל זג לוקה שתים - הא פלוגתא דאביי ורבא איתמר איפכא בפ' שלשה מינין (נזיר דף לח:), וכהנה רבות בגמרא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 41b:5:1.english: Rava said: [If] he ate a grape skin, he receives two [sets of lashes] - This dispute between Abaye and Rava is stated in the reverse in the chapter [entitled] Sheloshah Minim (Nazir 38b), and there are many [cases] like this in the Gemara.
